newsitem.title: USA: IRS halts "fast-pay" corporate financing deals-NYT.
newsitem.headline: IRS halts "fast-pay" corporate financing deals-NYT.

text.p: The U.S. Government has banned a popular corporate financing technique on Wall Street, effectively halting billions of dollars in borrowing transactions, the New York Times reported Friday.

The report said the technique centers on a type of security known as "fast pay" or "step down" preferred stock, which make tax advantages given to real estate investment trusts available to corporate borrowers.
The Internal Revenue Service on Thursday banned the technique after deciding that it was a tax dodge threatening to cause a major loss of revenue for the U.S. Treasury, the report said.
The report said one Treasury Department official estimated that as much as $20 billion in such deals had been completed or were under way.

It said some of the deals were arranged by investment bankers such as Morgan Stanley and Bear Stearns, but that the biggest borrower appears to have been the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp, better known as Freddie Mac, the private mortgage company sponsored by the U.S. Government.
